findings.reason: the section must be re-measured against current code, or its premise "that walk never reads sprint status at all" is false as written.
findings.text: §1 names `_derive_default_sprint_focus` in `reckon/project_state.py` as the offending walk, but that function does not exist at base `1aa17d0b`; it was replaced on 2026-09-25 (`bec9f24a7`) by `focus_sprint_id` (`reckon/project_state.py:1277`), which reads stored `active` status (lines 1295–1308). A reviewer and an implementer each open `project_state.py` and find no such function.

findings.reason: the plan would re-dispatch work whose shared derivation already exists, and its "done when" for the active-sprint pair is partly already met.
findings.text: §1 claims roadmap and `read_plan(project,"index")` compute `active_sprint_id` two different ways, but both now route through `focus_sprint_id`: `read_plan("index")` → `compose_project_state` (`reckon/_store.py:1545`, `project_state.py:1580`) and roadmap via `_sprint_status_buckets` (`reckon/roadmap.py:2248`). §1's defect is already closed for the status-active case.

findings.reason: §4/§5 build the ambiguity decision on an invariant the code has explicitly abandoned; "the read must refuse when two sprints carry active" contradicts the live design.
findings.text: §3 asserts the audit reports `multiple-active-sprints` at error severity as its only blocking finding, but that code does not exist anywhere in `reckon/`; `tests/test_sprint_push_keeps_both_active.py:92` asserts it must NOT fire, and its docstring states the finding is retired ("several active sprints are an ordinary scheduling state").

findings.reason: the section should extend/assert `focus_sprint_id` rather than add a parallel resolver, and must name it.
findings.text: the plan proposes one authority for `active_sprint_id`, but `focus_sprint_id` is that authority already and is imported by `reckon/roadmap.py:60`; a new resolution path beside it forks the owner, and the `work-scheduling-surface` sibling plan already records that "the two surfaces' agreement is not asserted anywhere" — the missing work is a run-side parity assertion over the existing owner, not a new reader.

findings.reason: the parity owner must be updated in the same change or the two disagree; naming it is the item's whole purpose.
findings.text: the plan's membership half re-derives "read the item list and the scalar and reconcile" without naming `project_state_parity.py`, whose `_sprint_membership` (232) and `ORGANISATIONAL_FIELDS["sprint"] (386) already read both copies and would follow any change of authority.

findings.reason: the section should be rewritten to extend `focus_sprint_id` for the residual case, not to re-add a status consult.
findings.text: §4's active-sprint repair duplicates behaviour `focus_sprint_id` already provides and offers no justification for adding a layer rather than extending it; the only genuine remainder (refusing on several active sprints) is exactly what the current design no longer wants (`tests/test_sprint_push_keeps_both_active.py`).

findings.reason: the section must account for the added refusal surface, especially since `multiple-active-sprints`, the finding it invokes, is itself retired — so the plan plausibly removes one finding while adding a refusal and never reconciles the two.
findings.text: the `ambiguous-active-sprint` and `membership-authority` decisions add refusal behaviour (refuse on read / refuse at write) without naming a refusal family they retire or merge, or stating why nothing can be; refusal_families is 23 this week.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan proposes no new module or wrapper family; the membership repair folds into `compose_project_state`, which already hides the store behind one call, so no shallow-wrapper spread is introduced.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan would add an active-sprint resolution path beside `reckon/project_state.py` (`focus_sprint_id`, `compose_project_state`) and a membership reconciliation path beside `reckon/project_state_parity.py` (`_sprint_membership`), instead of extending the owners that already read both copies.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1470, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §4 adds a refusal family (ambiguous-active read, membership refused at write) without naming in its own text what refusal or read it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites a derivation (`_derive_default_sprint_focus`, §1) that no longer exists, and claims no reader consults stored status, while `focus_sprint_id` (`reckon/project_state.py:1277`) already does and is already shared by roadmap and `read_plan(index)`, and the plan never cites `project_state_parity.py`, which already reads both membership copies.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §4's active-sprint repair ("the composed read must consult stored status rather than walking composed order") is already exactly what `focus_sprint_id` does, so the section as written adds a layer over machinery that already performs it, with no stated reason the existing derivation cannot be extended.
